subject.title: Several latent session/workspace lifecycle concurrency bugs (native-VNC credential leak, run-status stomp, terminal-hub races)

question: Should native-VNC grants fail closed when a session enters teardown or changes authorization/workspace identity during minting, matching the browser-VNC lifecycle boundary proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/crabfleet/pull/89?
rationale: The proposed behavior is a security-boundary choice with legitimate availability tradeoffs, and the issue is explicitly marked for security and maintainer review.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed lifecycle checks
options.body: Review the native-VNC change as the intended authorization boundary and require focused proof that valid live sessions still receive grants.

options.title: Narrow the boundary
options.body: Accept only a smaller status-based guard if maintainers intentionally do not want post-mint authorization and workspace-identity revalidation.

options.title: Defer the VNC change
options.body: Keep the issue and focused pull request open until the trust-boundary policy is explicitly decided.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed lifecycle checks
recommendation.body: Review the native-VNC change as the intended authorization boundary and require focused proof that valid live sessions still receive grants.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged session-scoped native-VNC feature identified in the supplied history.
